title: Weekly alignment + micro-OKR experiment log — Samantha Ortiz
content:
Week: Nov 6–12 2024
Owner: Sam Ortiz (personal OKR lane)

ONE-LINER OBJECTIVE
Keep momentum on the personal OKR to reduce context-switch tax and ship two meaningful infra-facing docs that clear ambiguity for the serving runtime team. Treat this week as a micro-experiment in focus and batching.

Top-3 Focuses (commitments)
1) Draft and publish 'KV-cache heuristics for heterogeneous workloads' doc — target length 700–1,000 words.
   - Success metric: doc published + shared in #serving-runtime by Fri EOB; 2 peer comments.
2) Reduce daily meeting time by 40% via time-blocking + asynchronous updates.
   - Success metric: calendar shows 3x 45–60 min deep-focus blocks and 0 reactive meetings added.
3) Ship a small automation to tag long-running requests in traces so we can rerun a 1-hour tail analysis.
   - Success metric: automation merged to infra repo + a scheduled job created in staging.

Weekly metrics snapshot (personal scoreboard)
- Deep focus hours target: 15h; actual (so far): 7.5h (midweek).
- Docs published: 0 -> target 1.
- Meetings trimmed: baseline 10hrs/wk -> targeted 6hrs; current scheduled 8hrs.
- Experiment runs for trace-tagging: 0 -> target 1 in staging.

Hypotheses for this micro-week
- H1: Blocking scheduling (three fixed deep-focus slots) will increase uninterrupted coding time and raise doc completion by 30%.
- H2: A 15-minute async status note in #serving-runtime will prevent 1 ad-hoc follow-up meeting per major change.
- H3: Tagging traces earlier in the pipeline reduces tail-analysis wall time by at least 20%.

Planned cadence & ritual
- Mon: Outline doc + rough bullets (1h deep block).
- Tue: Fill first 400 words + automation spike (2h).
- Wed: Review + send to Riley for quick read (1h).
- Thu: Iterate with feedback + schedule run in staging (2h).
- Fri: Finalize doc, post to channel, retro check.
Daily micro-commitments: 3 Pomodoro-style deep blocks (50/10) and one 30-min email/Slack sweep.

Current blockers / risks
- Risk: Oncall ping or infra incident could wipe out deep focus windows. Mitigation: set phone to DND & post calendar OOO for blocks.
- Unknown dependency: need sample trace data from SRE (ticket opened, waiting).
- Time bias: tendency to over-edit first draft; force-first-publish rule (v0 by Thu).

Notes-to-self (scratch)
- Keep doc pragmatic: quick examples > exhaustive measurement table.
- Use the 'examples' folder for sample traces, not inline heavy logs.
- If SRE doesn't supply traces by Wed EOD, use anonymized synthetic traces (generate via local runner).
- Tag Riley/Ava in doc for band-limited review (ask for quick 30-min pass).

Retro (last week quick reflections)
- Wins: Completed the 'cost-model sketch' and got 1 customer insight that reshaped prioritization. Felt momentum.
- Misses: Spent 6 hours in back-to-back syncs; wasted 3 focus blocks.
- Learnings: Blocked calendar + a short daily async update materially reduced late follow-ups.

Action items (concrete)
- [ ] Mon: Create doc outline in /personal/notes and link to repo issue — due 2024-11-07 (Sam).
- [ ] Tue: PR for trace-tagging spike with README — due 2024-11-08 (Sam).
- [ ] Wed: Send doc to Riley for quick read (comment by Thu) — due 2024-11-09 (Riley).
- [ ] Thu: Run staging job + capture first analysis snapshot — due 2024-11-11 (Sam & Ava).
- [ ] Fri: Publish doc to #serving-runtime and run retrospective notes — due 2024-11-12 (Sam).

Confidence & notes
- Confidence level: 6/10 (time pressure from cross-team priorities).
- If confidence drops below 4/10 by Wed AM, pivot: push doc to next week and prioritize trace-tagging only.

Random raw ideas (brain-dump)
- Could add a 'focus token' in calendar invites to mark true deep work; teammates can book only 10% of focus tokens.
- Explore automating the 'publish-to-channel' step via a small script that creates the message with doc link + TL;DR.

Unresolved questions
- Do we have existing instrumentation for trace sampling that I can reuse or will I need to add a new tag endpoint? (ask SRE).
- Best place for the final doc canonical location? internal docs vs notes repo. (prefer internal docs for discoverability)

Slack seeds / draft announcement (to post when doc done)
"Heads up: published a short note on KV-cache heuristics for mixed workloads — link + 3 TL;DR bullets. Looking for tiny edits or quick calls if you see major gaps. Tag me or drop comments. — Sam"

End-of-week self-check (fill Friday)
- Deep focus hours achieved: ____
- Doc published? yes/no
- Trace automation merged? yes/no
- Main blocker still present? yes/no

Footer: personal log id: sam-2024-11-microokrs-1. Short, low-friction experiments > perfect, high-effort outputs.
